questions.chapter: Chapter 2: General Principles, Simulation Software & Queueing System Simulation
questions.text: Define System, Model, and Simulation. When is simulation appropriate and when is it not appropriate? Explain the steps in a Simulation Study (Problem formulation, Model conceptualization, Data collection, Model translation, Verification and Validation, Experimental design, Production runs, and Documentation).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to System Modeling & Discrete-Event Simulation Concepts
questions.text: Explain Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) components: Entities, Attributes, Activities, Events, Event List (FEL), System State, and Clock Mechanism (Time-advance algorithm). Manually simulate a Single-Server Queuing System ($M/M/1$) for 6 customer arrivals showing simulation clock, event list, queue status, and server utilization.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to System Modeling & Discrete-Event Simulation Concepts
questions.text: Explain Kendall's notation for queuing systems ($A/B/c/N/K$). Derive formulas for steady-state probabilities $P_n = (1-\rho)\rho^n$, Average number of customers in system ($L = \frac{\lambda}{\mu - \lambda}$), Average waiting time in queue ($W_q = \frac{\lambda}{\mu(\mu - \lambda)}$) for an $M/M/1$ queue with arrival rate $\lambda$ and service rate $\mu$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Random Number Generation Techniques (LCG) & Random Variate Generation (Inverse Transform, Acceptance-Rejection)
questions.text: Explain properties of Pseudo-Random Numbers (Uniformity and Independence). Explain Linear Congruential Generator (LCG): $X_{i+1} = (a X_i + c) \bmod m$. Generate a sequence of 5 random numbers between $0$ and $1$ using Mixed LCG with $a = 7, c = 5, m = 64$, and seed $X_0 = 3$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Random Number Generation Techniques (LCG) & Random Variate Generation (Inverse Transform, Acceptance-Rejection)
questions.text: Explain statistical tests for Pseudo-Random numbers: (a) Chi-Square Frequency Test for uniformity ($\chi^2 = \sum \frac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}$), (b) Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) Test, and (c) Runs Test for independence (Runs above/below the mean and Runs up/down).

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Random Number Generation Techniques (LCG) & Random Variate Generation (Inverse Transform, Acceptance-Rejection)
questions.text: Explain the Inverse Transform Technique for generating random variates. Derive the inverse transform formula for generating: (a) Exponentially distributed variates ($X = -\frac{1}{\lambda} \ln(1 - R)$), (b) Uniformly distributed variates, and (c) Triangular distribution.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Statistical Models in Simulation & Input Data Modeling
questions.text: Differentiate between Model Verification (building the model right) and Model Validation (building the right model). Explain calibration and validation of simulation models using Naylor and Finger's 3-step validation approach (Face validity, Validation of model assumptions, Validating input-output transformations with historical data using Turing test).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: General Principles, Simulation Software & Queueing System Simulation
questions.text: Differentiate between Terminating Simulation and Non-Terminating (Steady-State) Simulation. How is Initialization Bias / Warm-up Period handled using Welch's graphical method and Batch Means method for output analysis?

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to System Modeling & Discrete-Event Simulation Concepts
questions.text: Differentiate between: (a) Static vs Dynamic simulation models, (b) Deterministic vs Stochastic models, and (c) Discrete vs Continuous simulation models with engineering examples.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Random Number Generation Techniques (LCG) & Random Variate Generation (Inverse Transform, Acceptance-Rejection)
questions.text: Explain Acceptance-Rejection Method and Box-Muller Transformation for generating Standard Normal random variates from uniform random numbers: $Z_1 = \sqrt{-2\ln R_1}\cos(2\pi R_2)$ and $Z_2 = \sqrt{-2\ln R_1}\sin(2\pi R_2)$.
